Track changes: <trace><para><ital>The Carbon Capture and Storage Act</ital><footnote><para> John Stefaniuk, “Not Just Hot Air: Manitoba Introduces The Captured Carbon Storage Act” (11 June 2024), online (article): https://www.tdslaw.com/resource/not-just-hot-air-manitoba-introduces-the-captured-carbon-storage-act/</para></footnote></para><para>Manitoba Bill 31, known as <ital>the Carbon Capture and Storage Act</ital> (CCS Act), represents a significant legislative effort to combat climate change through the regulation and promotion of carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies. Introduced in the Manitoba Legislature, this bill aims to provide a comprehensive legal framework for the development, implementation, and management of CCS projects within the province. </para><para>Bill 31, <ital>The Carbon Capture and Storage Act</ital> (CCS Act) also aligns with federal CO2 emission credits allowing a cohesive strategy for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The federal government has implemented a carbon pricing system that includes a carbon tax and an output-based pricing system (OBPS) for large industrial emitters. The CCS Act in Manitoba complements these federal efforts by:</para><para>Compliance Reducing Costs: CCS projects developed under the CCS Act can significantly reduce the carbon emissions of industrial facilities. This reduction helps these facilities lower their carbon tax liabilities or receive credits under the OBPS, which sets a cap on emissions and provides credits for staying below that cap.</para><para>Generating Emission Credits: By capturing and storing CO2, facilities can generate emission reduction credits. These credits can be traded or used to meet federal compliance obligations, integrating seamlessly with the federal carbon pricing system.</para><para>The primary objectives of the Carbon Capture and Storage Act are to establish a legal and regulatory framework for CCS activities, ensure the safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible implementation of CCS projects, promote investment in CCS technologies and infrastructure within Manitoba, and align provincial climate policies with national and international greenhouse gas reduction commitments.</para><para>The enactment of Bill 31 positions Manitoba as a leader in climate change mitigation through innovative technologies. By providing a structured approach to CCS, the province aims to reduce its carbon footprint and contribute to Canada’s national emissions reduction targets, attract investment in clean technology and green infrastructure, potentially boosting the local economy, and set a precedent for other provinces and regions to develop similar legislative frameworks for CCS</para></trace>
